In [[numerical linear algebra]], the '''Chebyshev iteration''' is an
[[Iterative method#Linear systems|iterative method]] for determining the solutions of a [[system of linear equations]]. The method is named after [[Russia]]n mathematician [[Pafnuty Chebyshev]].

Chebyshev iteration avoids the computation of [[inner product]]s as is necessary for the other nonstationary methods. For some distributed-memory architectures these inner products are a bottleneck with respect to efficiency. The price one pays for avoiding inner products is that the method requires enough knowledge about spectrum of the coefficient matrix&nbsp;''A'', that is an upper estimate for the upper [[eigenvalue]] and lower estimate for the lower eigenvalue.  There are modifications of the method for nonsymmetric matrices&nbsp;''A''.

==Example code in [[MATLAB]]==

<syntaxhighlight lang="matlab">
function [x] = SolChebyshev002(A, b, x0, iterNum, lMax, lMin)

  d = (lMax + lMin) / 2;
  c = (lMax - lMin) / 2;
  preCond = eye(size(A)); % Preconditioner
  x = x0;
  r = b - A * x;

  for i = 1:iterNum % size(A, 1)
      z = linsolve(preCond, r);
      if (i == 1)
          p = z;
          alpha = 1/d;
      else if (i == 2)
          beta = (1/2) * (c * alpha)^2
          alpha = 1/(d - beta / alpha);
          p = z + beta * p;
      else
          beta = (c * alpha / 2)^2;
          alpha = 1/(d - beta / alpha);
          p = z + beta * p;
      end;

      x = x + alpha * p;
      r = b - A * x; %(= r - alpha * A * p)
      if (norm(r) < 1e-15), break; end; % stop if necessary
  end;
end
</syntaxhighlight>
